ruleset.name: Phlix-Shared-Tests
ruleset.description:
PSR-12 for tests/, minus two sniffs that PSR-12 does not actually require of test code. This file is DELIBERATELY separate from the src/ gate (`phpcs --standard=PSR12 src/`), which stays untouched: src/ keeps full PSR-12 with zero exclusions and zero warnings.
THE MEASUREMENT THAT CHOSE THESE TWO EXCLUSIONS (master @ 1880888, phpcs 3.13.5, one-off `--standard=PSR12 tests/ --report=summary` plus `--report=source` runs — the totals footer and per-sniff table quoted below are `summary`/`source` report output, not what the CI gate's default `full` report prints):
A TOTAL OF 360 ERRORS AND 28 WARNINGS WERE FOUND IN 44 FILES
PSR1.Methods.CamelCapsMethodName ............... 354 (98.3% of errors) PSR1.Classes.ClassDeclaration.MultipleClasses .. 6 everything else ................................ 0 (+ 28 warnings: all Generic.Files.LineLength)
`phpcbf --standard=PSR12 tests/` reports "No fixable errors were found" — not one of the 360 errors is tooling-fixable, so "run phpcbf and commit" was never on the table. The two sniff exclusions below account for ALL 360 errors; with them applied the corpus is 0 errors and 28 warnings. There is no baseline and no ignore list beyond these two lines.
1. PSR1.Methods.CamelCapsMethodName — 354 errors, and all 354 were classified rather than assumed: 304 distinct method names, 348 hits on `test_*` PHPUnit cases and 6 on `provide_*` data-provider methods referenced by name-string in @dataProvider annotations (all six in tests/Relay/RelayFrameTest.php). ZERO were leading-uppercase and ZERO were already camelCase, so this is ONE deliberate snake_case convention, not accumulated sloppiness. PSR-12 §4.3 governs the declared API of production classes; PHPUnit discovers test methods by the `test` prefix, they read as sentences, and snake_case is a mainstream PHPUnit style. Renaming 304 methods would break every `--filter` expression and @depends/@dataProvider reference pointing at them, and would buy nothing. src/ is unaffected: it passes this sniff today with 0 errors.
2. PSR1.Classes.ClassDeclaration.MultipleClasses — 6 errors. Five are in-file fixture classes co-located in tests/Arr/ client tests (Prowlarr/Radarr/Sonarr/RadarrCrud/Bazarr), one is an in-file trait at tests/Support/PayloadAssertTest.php. Keeping a double next to its only consumer holds it out of the autoloadable namespace. Splitting six files' doubles into six-plus new files makes the suite harder to read, not more correct.
WARNINGS ARE REPORTED AND DO NOT BLOCK — and the difference from `-n` matters. Measured on the pinned 3.13.6 (2026-10-02, throwaway single-violation probes): the exit trigger is `errors + warnings > 0`, so WARNINGS ALONE exit non-zero — a lone non-fixable LineLength warning exits 1 — and the 1-vs-2 split is FIXABILITY, not warning-vs-error (1 = violations found, none phpcbf-fixable; 2 = at least one fixable). A gate that trusts its exit code would therefore be permanently red here at exit 1 over the 28 pre-existing LineLength warnings (long lines in generated-pin fixtures, none of them fixable), and the next person would silence it with `-n`. Re-measure this sentence on any phpcs major bump. That is precisely the defect this ruleset's existence prevents: `-n` on the src/ CI step SUPPRESSED warnings from both the report and the exit math until 2026-10-02. So the `ignore_warnings_on_exit` config below is set instead — it changes only the exit code. Every warning is still counted and still printed in the job log, and the per-file "FOUND n ERRORS … AFFECTING m LINES" footers of the default `full` report are the lines to read there. No "A TOTAL OF" line ever appears in this job's log — that footer belongs to the `summary` report, which the CI invocation (`--standard=phpcs-tests.xml --colors`) never requests; a grep for it could never fire. The gate is phpcs's nonzero exit code, read directly by the runner, not a log line (see phlix-server .github/workflows/coding-standards.yml @ 4c96f085). Do NOT add `-n` and do NOT exclude Generic.Files.LineLength; warnings stay visible here and src/ fails on them outright.
Anything added to the exclude list needs the same treatment: a count, a classification of what the violations actually ARE, and a reason PSR-12 does not require it of test code.
